::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[For matrices $2 \times 2$, conditions for $A$ such that $tr(XAY^{T})$ is an inner product](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/3342068/for-matrices-2-times-2-conditions-for-a-such-that-trxayt-is-an-inne), asked by [Alexandre Tourinho](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/557910/alexandre-tourinho) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2019-09-02; [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)):

> Given a generic $2 \times 2$ matrix $A$:
>
> $$\left[
> \begin{array}{cc}
>   a&b\\
>   c&d
> \end{array}
> \right]$$
>
> the exercise is to determine conditions for $a$, $d$ and $b-c$ such that $tr(XAY^{T})$ is an inner product.
>
> Verifying linearity and symmetry we get $b=c$.
>
> My problem is verifying the positive-definite propertie. I arrived at the expression, where $x_1, x_2, x_3, x_4$ are the elements of the matrix $X$:
>
> $tr(XAX^{T}) = a(x_1^2+x_3^2) + d(x_2^2+x_4^2) + (b+c)(x_1x_2 + x_3x_4)$
>
> but was unable to analyse the conditions $a$ and $d$ should satisfie.
:::

Completing the square should help here.  For instance,
$$\begin{align*}
    ax_1^2 + d x_2^2 + 2bx_1x_2 &= a\left(x_1 + \frac{b}{a}x_2\right)^2 + \left(d - \frac{b^2}{a}\right)x_3^2
\end{align*}$$
You want the coefficients of the squares on the right to be positive.
